steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ What happens in Scene 0? 

❓ When should the project pause until?


Solution:

In callScene(0), the pauseUntilAnyButtonIsPressed function should be moved above the destroyAllSpritesOfKind function so that the Splash sprites appear on screen until any button is pressed to begin the project directions.


Ask the ninja: 

❓ What happens in Scene 1? 

❓ Which arguments should be updated so that when the Cursor sprite overlaps each level’s image while the A button is pressed, the user is taken to the corresponding tilemap?


Solution:

In callScene(1), the sprite function variable should be used in the first overlapsWith function in the if condition. 


In callScene(1), the levelSelectMed image asset should be used in the image.equals function in the second if condition.


Ask the ninja: 

❓ What happens in Scene 5? 

❓ Which sound should be paused before the Game over screen is displayed? 

❓ Which sounds should play when the game ends in a win and a loss?


Solution:

In callScene(5), the stopAllSounds function should be used to stop the waveSong asset from being played, before the splashBackground image asset is displayed. The powerDown sound should be played if the game ends in a loss; the powerUp sound should be played if the game ends in a win.
steps.instructions:
Debug the code to create a working project by breaking down the errors into smaller chunks!


Pass different sceneNum values to the callScene function to identify the errors, one scene at a time.


The project title should be displayed on screen until the user presses a button to view the directions.


The user should be taken to the corresponding level’s tilemap after they make a selection on the Level Select screen.


The music played during a wave should stop and the corresponding sounds should play based on the outcome of the game, when the Game Over screen is displayed.


Use the functions in the code menu and the code completion tool to create a working version of this project! Focus on one scene at a time to debug the errors in small chunks.

In this level, you’ll apply your previous learning by creating a complex tower defense project in JavaScript across 4 different Build activities.
